profile.constituencyprofile_Text:
Kavali Assembly Constituency, located in the northern part of SPSR Nellore District, comprises Kavali, Bogole, Allur, and Dagadarthi Mandals, and includes the Kavali Municipality and Allur Nagara Panchayat. It falls under the Nellore Lok Sabha Constituency. With a total population of 2,89,461, around 68.87% reside in rural areas and 31.12% in urban regions, spread across 77,455 households. The constituency has a sex ratio of 997 females per 1,000 males and a literacy rate of 65.48%, with the workforce predominantly engaged in agriculture. The region's natural coastal geography, featuring a 48 km coastal belt, makes it a key contributor to fisheries and aquaculture in the district. It is also characterized by black cotton and red soils, with irrigation supported by Somasila Project canals and 102 minor irrigation tanks, enabling extensive paddy cultivation. Kavali is well-connected through NH-16 (Chennai–Kolkata) and NH-67, and its railway station on the Howrah–Chennai main line enhances transport access. Its strategic location near the upcoming Ramayapatnam Port and Juvvaladinne fishing harbor strengthens its potential for trade and industrial development. 

The constituency has educational and health infrastructure, including 277 primary schools, 77 high schools, 1 polytechnic, 3 engineering colleges, 2 area hospitals, 52 rural PHCs, 6 urban PHCs, and 4 community health centres. Rich in cultural heritage, the region is home to landmarks such as the Sri Prasanna Venkateswara Swamy Temple, Poleramma Thalli Temple, and scenic spots like Thummalapenta and Iskapalli Beaches. With its natural resources, infrastructure, and upcoming port connectivity, Kavali is well-positioned to achieve an ambitious 15% annual growth across major sectors.

economy_text.economy_Text:
With a Gross Constituency Domestic Product (GCDP) of ₹8,730 crores in 2023-24 (FRE), Kavali Assembly Constituency is projected to grow to ₹1,80,887 crores by 2047-48, reflecting a strong and sustainable annual growth trajectory of 12–15%. This historic economic transformation will be fueled by strategic investments in infrastructure, industrialization, services expansion, and agricultural modernization.

The fisheries sub-sector holds significant potential, contributing ₹1,638 crores (20.28% of GCVA in 2023-24) through marine and inland aquaculture production. Meanwhile, the services sector—currently the largest contributor to GCVA at 40.45% (₹3,267 crores)—is expected to rise to 54.06% by 2047-48, emerging as the primary engine of economic growth.

High-growth sub-sectors such as transport, real estate, banking and finance, trade, hospitality, education, and tourism are projected to expand at an annual rate of 13–15%. Kavali is thus poised to evolve from a primarily regional economy into a high-value industrial, commercial, and services-driven hub..
